memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Do not muzzle an ox while it is treading out the grain. - Deut 25:4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This short verse carries a surprisingly rich meaning. As an ox worked, treading grain to separate it, it was not to be muzzled but allowed to eat some of the grain as it laboured. It was only fair that the animal doing the work should share in the fruit of that work. God's compassion and sense of fairness extended even to a working animal.

But this verse means even more than kindness to animals. The apostle Paul quotes this exact command twice in the New Testament, applying it to how those who labour in ministry should be supported. He argues that just as the ox deserves to eat from its work, so those who work hard preaching and teaching deserve to be provided for (1 Cor 9:9-11; 1 Tim 5:17-18). The principle is that a worker deserves the fruit of their labour.

There are two lovely truths here. First, God cares about fairness, that those who work should share in the benefits of their work, and should not be exploited or deprived of their due. Second, God's people are to generously support those who labour for the gospel. This challenges us to be fair and generous, never taking advantage of others' work, and to gladly support those who serve us spiritually. How can you make sure you are being fair to those who work for and around you, and generous toward those who serve you in the faith?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you fair to those who work for and around you?
2. Do you generously support those who serve you spiritually?
3. Where might you be tempted to deprive someone of their due?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You care about fairness and provision for workers. Help me be fair and generous, honouring the labour of others. Amen.
